what_its_for: Tivozanib is a cancer medicine used to treat advanced kidney cancer (renal cell carcinoma). It works by blocking signals that help tumors grow new blood vessels, which slows or stops the cancer from growing and spreading.
how_to_take: Swallow the capsule whole with or without food. Do not open, crush, or chew the capsule. Take it at the same time each day to help you remember. If you vomit after taking a dose, do not take another dose that day — just take your next scheduled dose the following day.
dosing: The usual dose is one 1.34 mg capsule taken by mouth once a day for 21 days (3 weeks), followed by 7 days off (no medicine). This 28-day cycle is then repeated. Your doctor may lower your dose or pause treatment if you have side effects. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and there are more than 12 hours left until your next scheduled dose, take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is less than 12 hours until your next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses in one day to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store tivozanib capsules at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep them in the original container with the lid tightly closed. Protect from moisture and heat. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush medicines down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of unused capsules.
what_to_avoid: Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice, as they can increase the amount of this medicine in your blood and cause more side effects. Avoid St. John's Wort (an herbal supplement), as it can make tivozanib less effective. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before starting any new prescription medicines, over-the-counter drugs, vitamins, or herbal supplements, as many can interact with tivozanib. Avoid becoming pregnant while taking this medicine — use reliable birth control during treatment and for at least 1 month after your last dose.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: very high blood pressure or severe headache; signs of bleeding such as coughing up blood, blood in your urine or stool, or unusual bruising; chest pain, shortness of breath, or signs of a heart attack or stroke; severe diarrhea, nausea, or vomiting that you cannot control; signs of liver problems such as yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe stomach pain; unusual tiredness or weakness; mouth sores that are severe or painful; signs of a wound that is not healing; or any new or worsening symptoms that concern you.
when_it_works: Tivozanib may start to slow cancer growth fairly quickly, but you may not feel or notice the effects right away. Your doctor will monitor your progress with regular imaging scans and blood tests to see how well the medicine is working. It is important to keep taking it as prescribed even if you do not feel different.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tivozanib can harm an unborn baby. Do not use during pregnancy. Women who can become pregnant should use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 1 month after the last dose. Men with female partners who can become pregnant should also use birth control during treatment and for 1 month after the last dose. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine or for at least 1 month after the last dose. Kidney or liver problems: Your doctor may adjust your dose if you have moderate to severe liver problems. Tell your doctor about all your health conditions before starting this medicine. Older adults: This medicine has been studied in older adults and can generally be used safely, but you may be monitored more closely for side effects.
